dossier.public_summary: The dip depth alternates between odd and even eclipses and changes dramatically from sector to sector, with most of the signal coming from just a couple of deep events. This pattern matches a stellar eclipse on a binary or nearby star, not a steady small-planet transit on the target.

reasons.why: Odd and even transits differ at 4.462 sigma with 271.6 ppm difference (64% deeper odd), favouring an eclipsing binary at twice the period (28.8 d) over a planet where depths must match.

Depth is not steady: inconsistent even within the same pipeline product, with shallow sectors consistent with zero and deep sectors driven by a few events, as expected for a blended/crowded eclipsing signal rather than a planet.
reasons.value: verdict changes_within_a_source p_constant_all 1.387e-20, SPOC 2-min p_constant 1.9302178704787675e-16, depths 534, 1098, 47, 62, 477, -18, 624 ppm

reasons.why: Transit-to-transit depths are wildly inconsistent and dominated by the top few deep events; a true planet should be consistent and not have a 7-sigma outlier.
